questions.prompt: In ORM mapping, a C# class maps to a table and an object maps to a row. What does a property of the class map to?
questions.explanation: The mapping table pairs class ↔ table, object ↔ row, property ↔ column, object reference ↔ foreign key and `List<T>` ↔ one-to-many relation.

questions.prompt: You want EF Core to talk to SQL Server. Which package do you need to install?
options: `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer`, which also brings in the core library
No package; EF Core is built into .NET
questions.explanation: Installing `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` alone is not sufficient; you also need a database provider such as `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer`, and installing the provider automatically installs the core library.

source.section: ### Install EF Core to use in Application

questions.prompt: In `EFContext`, what is the role of `public DbSet<Product> Products { get; set; }`?
options: It represents the `Products` table and offers methods such as `Add`, `Attach` and `Remove`
It holds the connection string for the database
It runs the migrations when the app starts
It defines the database provider used by `OnConfiguring`
questions.explanation: A `DbSet<TEntity>` represents a table; it provides `Add`, `Attach`, `Remove` and so on, and the context maps those operations to SQL run through the database provider.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for creating a database with EF Core Code-First in the order the lesson follows.
steps: Create the `Product` entity class (a public POCO)
Create `EFContext : DbContext` with a `DbSet<Product>` property and the connection string in `OnConfiguring`
Run `Add-Migration "NewDatabase"` in the Package Manager Console
Run `Update-Database` to apply the migration and create the database
questions.explanation: With the model, context and `DbSet` ready, migrations create the database: `Add-Migration` generates the instructions, then `Update-Database` uses them and creates the database if it doesn't exist.

questions.prompt: A generated migration has an `Up()` and a `Down()` method. When is `Down()` used?
options: When the app starts, to drop and recreate tables
Only when the database does not exist yet
When rolling back, to remove the tables, columns and constraints that `Up()` created
questions.explanation: `Up()` creates tables, columns and constraints; `Down()` removes them and is used when rolling back.
